newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila o/night money tightens on heightened demand. [CORRECTED 12:13 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Manila o/night money tightens on heightened demand. [CORRECTED 12:13 GMT]

text.p: The Philippine overnight money tightened on Monday, with the average interbank call loan rate rising to 11.09375 percent from 10.8125 percent, after banks paid taxes and bought dollars last week, traders said.

More than 10 billion pesos were drained from the system after banks remitted value-added tax to the government and Central Bank sold dollars worth 3.5 billion pesos (corrects currency) in the past few days, one trader estimated.
"Most of the big banks were on the borrowing side," another trader said.
Total volume turnover swelled to 28.278 billion pesos with 29 lending institutions against 33 borrowers. Traders predicted the rates to soften in the coming days.
The secondary market for longer-termed securities was quiet with one-year bills being aggressively offered amidst small appetite from investors.
Banks were expecting one-year bills to rise at this afternoon's auction, following a sharp fall last week.
Three-month bills were being bid at 11.50 to 11.6 percent, and offered at 11.4 to 11.45 percent.
Six-month bills were being bid at 11.8 to 12.0 percent, and offered at 11.7 to 11.85 percent, while the one-year bills at 12.175 to 12.45 and offered at 12.075 to 12.30 percent.
Traders expected the shorter-termed rates to remain stable in this afternoon's auction, except for the one-year bills which many said could rise by 10 to 15 basis points.
